faq.q: Why does sand heat faster than water?
faq.a: Sunlight only warms the top of the sand, and water mixes the heat deep down. So sand heats and cools faster.
On most sunny days. Big weather like the monsoon can be stronger.

knowledgePack: Land heats up and cools down faster than water. By day, the land is warmer than the sea, air over the land warms and rises, and cooler air from the sea flows in near the ground: a sea breeze. At night the land cools below the sea's temperature and the flow reverses: a land breeze. Breezes are local and strongest on sunny, calm days. They always come from the cooler surface. In Mumbai the sea is west; in Chennai the sea is east. Larger weather systems like the monsoon can override breezes.
